draft.title: Continuity and change in beliefs
card: Continuity means a belief or practice stays the same over time. Change means it is altered, added to or dropped.
Contact with other ideas can change beliefs. When cultures meet through migration, trade or conflict, people may adopt, adapt or reject new ideas.
New technology and social change can also reshape beliefs. The internet lets a faith reach people far away, and shifts in social views may lead a group to rethink its teachings.
Many traditions stay strong at the same time. Rituals, texts and festivals can be passed on for generations, and a belief system often shows both continuity and change.
draft.remember: Beliefs can change through new contact, technology and society, and many traditions still last.

a.q: A religious community keeps its weekly service and ancient texts, but now streams the service online. What does this show?
opts: Both continuity and change in the same belief system
Continuity only, as the texts and service are unchanged
Change only, as streaming replaces the old practice
The belief system is being dropped by its members
a.why: The service and texts continue, which is continuity. Streaming is a change linked to new technology. Calling it change only is tempting, but the traditions still remain.
a.clue: Look at what stays the same and what is new.

b.q: Priya's family moved from India to Perth. They still hold their yearly festival, but now share it with neighbours of other faiths and have changed some customs. Which explanation fits best?
opts: Contact with other ideas changed customs as the festival lasted
The festival ended because the family left their home country
Migration always forces families to give up their traditions
New technology alone changed the customs, not contact
b.why: Living among people of other faiths is contact with other ideas, which may lead to some change. The festival is still held, so a tradition continues. Saying migration always ends traditions is wrong, as the card says many traditions stay strong.
b.clue: Does the festival still happen, and who has the family met?
